goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:228 — Routing CombinedRule abilities through the ruler-only helper drops the existing federated-group guard, allowing federated rules to expose edit/delete actions.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, the old `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` function (lines 203-275 in the original) contained logic to check `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used that to determine if a rule was immutable. The new `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` function (starting around line 228) now calls `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, and in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the federated check is commented out with `// TODO: Add support for federated rules` and `const isFederated = false;` is hardcoded. This means federated rules that were previously protected from edit/delete actions will now incorrectly show those actions because the `isFederated` guard is always false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — Prometheus-only Grafana list items can show “Silence notifications”, but no drawer is rendered because `rule` is absent, so clicking it has no effect.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer at line 104 is rendered with `rulerRule={rule}` where `rule` is the RulerRuleDTO. When only promRule is provided (no rulerRule), the drawer receives undefined. The AlertRuleMenu component checks canSilence using both ruler and grafana prom abilities (lines 91-92 in AlertRuleMenu.tsx show `canSilence = (silenceSupported && silenceAllowed) || (grafanaSilenceSupported && grafanaSilenceAllowed)`), so the Silence menu item can appear when only promRule exists. However, when the user clicks Silence, the drawer opens with `rulerRule={rule}` which would be undefined, causing the drawer to not function properly. This is a real bug where the UI shows an actionable menu item that doesn't work correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:287 — The Grafana-Prometheus ability table duplicates the ruler ability table, so new action-policy changes can silently diverge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate ability tables being created - useAllRulerRuleAbilities (lines 225-275) and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (lines 282-340). Both define the same AlertRuleAction mappings but with slightly different implementations. For example, useAllRulerRuleAbilities uses 'rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)' while useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses 'prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)'. The finding correctly identifies that maintaining two parallel ability tables creates a maintenance burden where changes to one might not be reflected in the other. This is a legitimate architectural concern about code duplication that could lead to divergent behavior, though it's not a bug per se - it's a design issue that could cause future problems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:191 — The new prom-only menu test omits Delete, so it cannot catch that delete is unavailable when `rulerRule` is absent despite delete permission.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real gap in test coverage. Looking at the test at line 82-119 ('should render More button with action menu options' and 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked'), the test verifies 4 menu items (silence, copyLink, duplicate, export) but does NOT verify that Delete is present or absent. The diff shows that the component now uses useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities which checks abilities based on promRule only (without rulerRule). The test grants delete permissions but doesn't verify the Delete menu item appears. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for the new permission-checking logic, though it's not a bug in the production code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:296 — No test covers a Prometheus rule with `provenance`, leaving the new immutable-rule permission behavior unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `isProvisionedPromRule` function at line 171 in rules.ts which checks `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) && Boolean(promRule.provenance)`. This is used in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` at line 296 to determine if a rule is immutable. Looking at the test file GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the tests use `grafanaRulerGroup` from mocks but don't specifically test the provenance path. The finding correctly identifies that the new provisioned rule behavior via `isProvisionedPromRule` lacks test coverage - no test creates a GrafanaPromRuleDTO with a `provenance` field set to verify the immutable rule logic works correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:65 — No test asserts that the list makes no Ruler request, so the central removal of that request can regress unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the GrafanaGroupLoader component was refactored to remove the Ruler API call (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery was removed from the imports and usage). The test file was updated but none of the tests verify that no Ruler requests are made. The finding correctly identifies that the central architectural change (removing Ruler requests from the list view) lacks test coverage to prevent regression. This is a valid concern about missing test coverage for a significant behavioral change, though it's not a bug since the code works as intended.
